# `Q-12-11` — Mixed Category Modes On One Page

> Two or more listings on the same page declare different
> `categories:` modes; the first non-disabled mode in
> declaration order wins for the rendered sidebar.

## What this means

The `categories:` key on a listing controls how categories are
collected and displayed in the categories sidebar — possible
modes include the default tag-cloud-style view, an unnumbered
list, a numbered count view, and outright disabling the
sidebar. Quarto renders one sidebar per page, so when multiple
listings on the same page disagree on the mode, only one mode
can apply.

The chosen mode is the first non-disabled one in declaration
order. The other listings still contribute their items to the
category set, but their preferred display mode is overridden.

## Why this happens

A page hosts more than one listing (a `listings:` array, or a
host page that includes a sub-document also configured as a
listing), and the entries declare different `categories:`
values.

## How to fix

Decide which mode you want for the page's sidebar and set the
same `categories:` value on every listing that contributes to
it. If a listing should not affect the sidebar, set its
`categories: false`.

## Related

- `Q-12-12` — categories enabled but no item declares any: the
  sidebar collapses to empty rather than overriding modes.
